items.followUp: When is the zero error of a screw gauge positive?

rubric.why: The zero error is observed with the screw gauge closed.
rubric.description: State that the jaws are closed.
rubric.how: Award this mark when the answer gives the closed-jaw condition.

rubric.why: Identifies the position of the circular-scale zero that gives negative zero error.
rubric.description: The zero of the circular scale lies above the reference line.
rubric.how: Award this mark when the answer correctly states that the circular-scale zero is above the reference line.

modelAnswer: Close the jaws of the screw gauge.
The zero error is negative when the zero of the circular scale lies above the reference line.

rubric.why: Identifies distance as the total length of the path travelled.
rubric.description: Distance is the total length of the path travelled and has magnitude only.
rubric.how: Award this mark for defining distance as the total path length.

rubric.why: Identifies displacement as a directed straight-line change in position.
rubric.description: Displacement is the shortest straight-line distance from the initial to the final position in a specified direction.
rubric.how: Award this mark for defining displacement as the straight-line change from initial to final position with direction.

modelAnswer: Distance is the total length of the path travelled and has magnitude only.
Displacement is the shortest straight-line distance from the initial to the final position in a specified direction.

rubric.why: Distinguishes positive acceleration by the increase in velocity.
rubric.description: Positive acceleration increases the velocity of a body with time.
rubric.how: Award this mark for linking positive acceleration to an increase in velocity or speed.

rubric.why: Distinguishes negative acceleration by the decrease in velocity and recognizes its alternate name.
rubric.description: Negative acceleration decreases the velocity of a body with time and is also called retardation.
rubric.how: Award this mark for linking negative acceleration to a decrease in velocity or speed.

modelAnswer: Positive acceleration increases the velocity of a body with time.
Negative acceleration decreases the velocity of a body with time and is also called retardation.
